note: Deterministic + reproducible. Keypairs from fixed seeds (A=0011..eeff, B=ffee..1100). canon=JCS tightened; H(tag,x)=sha256(ascii(tag)||0x00||x); content_hash=H("ust:state",canon({ust,state})); key_id=H("ust:keylog",raw_pub); partition_hash=H("ust:shard",canon({domain_shard,ust_id,partition,value})) — UNIFORM, every partition binds domain_shard, name is a VALUE (non-colliding), no domain-less computed. Each vector states the SPEC rule it pins. Signature-type vectors use expect: 'VALID' | 'E-SIG' for the Ed25519 PRIMITIVE check (strict, canonical-S); this is not a document verdict — a conforming verifier's document verdict is always tier-qualified (VALID:LIGHT/HIGH/TOP), never a bare VALID. Partition names inside hash/commit inputs (e.g. 'secret') are arbitrary sample names, not protocol features.

what_a_vector_pins._: WHAT A VECTOR MAY PIN — read this before excluding the `vector` layer of a round, and before deciding a case "cannot be a vector". Derived from THIS corpus on 2026-08-10, not declared: 228 vectors across 43 kinds.
what_a_vector_pins.the_rule: A vector is a FIXED INPUT and a DECLARED RESULT that a runner must reproduce. The input being a DOCUMENT is one case among several; the result being a VERDICT is one case among several.

measured_2026_08_10._how_these_were_counted: THREE of these are re-derived on every run by the UST#147 checks (total, kinds, forms) and cannot drift. `input_is_a_document` counts vectors carrying a `doc` field and `input_is_a_genesis_plus_log` counts those carrying a `genesis` field — both reproduced on 2026-08-10 while adding the round-138/139/142 vectors, which is how the second one moved from 59 to 63. `input_is_a_value_or_string` and `input_is_raw_bytes` are the counts recorded when this definition was first derived, and THEIR FORMULA WAS NEVER WRITTEN DOWN: neither a field scan nor a kind roster reproduces 75 or 27. They were left untouched here rather than quietly re-fitted, because a number adjusted to survive a gate is worse than a number that admits it cannot be re-derived. Note also that a count keyed to a FIELD is not a count keyed to MEANING — the four stream vectors added in round 198 take documents as input and do not appear under `input_is_a_document`, because their documents arrive in `frames`. Making every one of these derivable (a kind → form roster, so a new kind cannot exist outside the definition) is tracked as its own round.

what_a_vector_pins.when_the_layer_may_be_excluded: Only when the subject is NOT DETERMINISTIC — a live network, a registry read, wall-clock time, a published state that changes under you. It is NOT enough that the input is awkward to write down as JSON: a vector may NAME a scenario and let the runner build it from fixed seeds (form 8, see fork-visibility, which carries no input field at all). "There is no document to pin" is not a reason either — four of the forms above have none. An exclusion asserting impossibility must name WHICH of these forms the subject fails, and an existing kind that covers it refutes the exclusion.
what_a_vector_pins.history: The formula "Vectors pin document bytes and the verdicts they must produce" was used 46 times in tools/ladder-registry.json as a reason the layer could not exist. Measured against this corpus it describes 40 of 228. The two entries that widened the definition — faculty-absent-ed25519 (round 189) and ed25519-point-admission (round 190) — landed after all 46 were written. See UST#147. Round 196 added form 8 after the registry sweep found that several exclusions read "no fixed input" where the truth was "input not serialisable" — a distinction that decides whether a layer is closable.

vectors.rule: S9 content_hash = H("ust:state", canon({ust, state})) — the address every reference in this protocol resolves by
vectors.note: Round 200, and a NEW kind for a primitive that had none. `content_hash` is what `prev`, `based_on`, `constituents` and every anchor leaf denote, and no vector fixed it: the corpus pinned the hash of a PARTITION (`hash-partition-*`) and of a canonical string (`domainsep-*`), never of a whole document. Deliberately the SMALLEST admissible document — the point is the composition `H ∘ canon` over the two top-level members, not the richness of the state. A second implementation that canonicalised the document differently, or hashed `state` without `ust`, produces a different address for the same bytes and every reference silently misses.

round 139 — a document that neither IS nor EXTENDS the head is refused (self-fork: a sibling in an already-published slot)
vectors.note: CONSUMER FACE. Rounds 138/139/142 state a PRODUCER duty — what an operator must not emit. A vector cannot pin a duty, only bytes and the verdict they must produce, so what is pinned here is the duty's consumer face: the artifact the producer is forbidden to emit is REFUSED by any conforming verifier. The producer-side obligation stays in the operator suite (#124 F.5r-f/g/h), which is why the `test` layer of those rounds does not move. Frame 2 is a TWIN of frame 1, not a copy: same slot, same `prev`, DIFFERENT bytes — a producer that lost its head pointer and re-derived the interval from fresh input. A byte-identical re-publication would assert "the same document twice", which IS the head and is a different claim; the first draft of this fixture made exactly that mistake. HISTORY, kept because it is why this vector exists: before it, no vector in this corpus fed a same-slot twin to `verifyStream` at all — the whole input shape was unexercised. WHAT THIS VECTOR PINS IS THE REFUSAL, NOT THE ROUTE. Measured 2026-08-10 by removing the guards one at a time: this corpus's three refused stream inputs are caught at DIFFERENT depths — the sibling by four independent guards (duplicate `ust_id` → chronology → dangling prev → shared prev), the stale-head repeat by two (dangling prev → shared prev), and the headless frame by exactly ONE. A second implementation may refuse along any of them; requiring a particular one would pin OUR control flow instead of the protocol. The consequence for mutation testing is stated because it is not obvious: disabling any SINGLE guard leaves this vector green, so the honest control is directional — make refusal impossible and all three redden, make it unavoidable and the accepting control reddens instead.

vectors.note: CONSUMER FACE. Rounds 138/139/142 state a PRODUCER duty — what an operator must not emit. A vector cannot pin a duty, only bytes and the verdict they must produce, so what is pinned here is the duty's consumer face: the artifact the producer is forbidden to emit is REFUSED by any conforming verifier. The producer-side obligation stays in the operator suite (#124 F.5r-f/g/h), which is why the `test` layer of those rounds does not move. An absent `prev` is not a missing field, it is a claim: the stream begins here. Arriving after two published frames the claim is false, and a verifier that read it as "nothing to check" would let a producer silently re-origin its own stream. THIS INPUT IS THE ONE WITH NO SECOND LINE. Measured 2026-08-10: the sibling is caught by four guards and the stale-head repeat by two, but the headless frame is caught by the dangling-prev test ALONE — with that one branch removed the document is ADMITTED and the stream reads `provisional`, because the shared-prev guard is written `if (p && …)` and an absent `prev` is not a value it can compare. A guard with no backstop is exactly the one a second implementation is most likely to omit, and until this vector existed nothing in the corpus would have noticed. WHAT THIS VECTOR PINS IS THE REFUSAL, NOT THE ROUTE. vectors.rule: control for 138/139/142 — the SAME fixture, advanced from what was PUBLISHED, is accepted
vectors.note: Three refusals over one fixture prove nothing if the fixture itself cannot be accepted — they would be equally green against a verifier that refuses everything. Frame 2 here chains to frame 1, the repair the producer duty actually demands. `provisional` and not `complete`: no checkpoint is supplied, so the tail is open (P5). The corpus already carries this paired shape at `reroot-01`/`reroot-02`. Measured 2026-08-10, both directions: with every stream refusal removed the three negative vectors redden and this one stays green; with refusal made unavoidable this one reddens and the three stay green.

F.5z — a `reroot` naming its OWN genesis is a hash cycle, not a supersession
F.5z.5 — the witness log CARRIES the signed half on the entry it closes; a holder of the old genesis proves the successor from its own root key
F.5z.4 — a claim with no signed half is IGNORED, so the consumer does not follow; a refusal, never a stranding
F.5z — an identity nobody superseded says so; the positive vectors prove nothing without this control

S20/F.5p a profile with no declares object declares NOTHING and is not an error — every profile published before this section keeps working
S20.1/F.5o a copy declares a LOCATOR and nothing else — an independence coordinate offered alongside it is refused, never accepted and ignored
S20.1 a locator naming no artifact leaves the FETCHED party to say what it is a copy of

S14.1/F.5.1d a SUPPLY remedy is a promise refuted by the call that printed it — the same document verified WITH and WITHOUT genesis must not carry the same clause naming it. Measured live 2026-08-05: the two details were byte-identical, and the guard was the TIER, which does not imply the absence its sentence asserts

S14.1/F.5.1d the same invariant on the capacity axis, and the branch must stay REACHABLE for the vector to assert anything: a grant that is present AND usable removes the sentence entirely, so this vector supplies one that is present and UNUSABLE. The supply clause must vanish and the REPLACE clause must appear — silence would satisfy the first half alone and is not the theorem

S14.1/F.5.1d third site, and the one the gate could not SEE: keylogHeadAnchor reaches the core only by DESTRUCTURING, so an option roster built from opts.<name> missed it and an unguarded supply clause sat in the tree while the gate printed PASS. The guard here is freshness === unverified, which holds equally for an anchor supplied and not verified
S14.1/F.5p.2 a coordinate alone cannot say WHY it is low — the report pairs it with the inputs never supplied, so 'not asked' is distinguishable from 'asked and refused'
S14.1/F.5.1a a report may never tell a publisher its verdict would rise by supplying a CONSUMER faculty — those inputs carry the consumer term
S14.1 the report reads the CALL, not a rule table: an input actually supplied is attempted, never reported absent
S14.1/F.5.1b adding the report leaves every verdict identical — reading what would raise a document is not a step toward raising it

S14.1/F.5.1c a rung NOBODY can move is not a rung merely unmet: a key-form document binds its name by construction, so no input from either party raises the identity axis — the report must not list one as if it would

S14.1/F.5.1a a hint on a CONSUMER-faculty input must refuse rather than instruct: telling a publisher to supply one invites it to believe a tier no consumer will see — signed-not-true arriving through a help message
S19/F.5.1a-bis a well-formed document from a newer MINOR is not broken — the verifier's ruleset is what is missing, so the answer is INDETERMINATE(unsupported_minor), never INVALID
S19/F.5.1a-bis a different MAJOR leaves the verifier nothing to evaluate — that is a REACH limit, not a byte defect. Minor and major differ in reach, never in validity
S19/F.5t the whole point: a correct newer document and a corrupt one must NOT produce the same observation — before this they were byte-identical INVALID/E-MALFORMED
S19 a minor only ADDS, so an older document verifies unchanged on a newer verifier — the backward half of the contract

S14/F.5.1a-bis THE LINE: INVALID means 'I applied MY rules and they were violated'. A ruleset the verifier lacks is outside that sentence, so neither a future minor nor a foreign major may share a verdict with corruption

S14.1/F.5.1 no-fork evidence belongs to an INDEPENDENT WITNESS, not to the publisher: self-attestation that no rival genesis exists is worth nothing, and a column with only publisher/consumer silently instructs an operator to produce what it is barred from producing

F.5t-a The obligation is a property of a SET. A member that wears the protocol name and is not a document of it is REPORTED and named by its id — a tally without the offending member is a number an operator cannot act on
F.5t-a The rule forbids wearing the name without BEING a document, never wearing it: a set whose named members are documents is compliant

F.5t-a An empty target set satisfies a universal quantifier for free, so it is its own outcome and never folded into compliance — a wrong path is how a mirror nobody looked at reads as a clean one (F.5p: absence is two facts)
F.5t-a A set that examined artifacts and found NONE wearing the name is distinguishable from one that examined none: four outcomes, never three
F.5t-a FAIL CLOSED: an artifact that wears the name and cannot be parsed is the case the rule is about, not an exemption from it — a consumer meeting it gets E-MALFORMED, which is F.5t's subject

F.5t-a A parsed artifact is judged from its TOP LEVEL and nothing else. A served list — a key log, an index — has no top level to make the claim with, and a marker inside one of its entries is not the list claiming it. The byte scan exists only where there IS no top level
F.5q-c The granularity is READ from the window fields, so a coarser committer is not mistaken for a silent one. No declaration appears in the expression
F.5q-c The two answers a publisher's silence used to collapse into one must differ: covered-by-a-coarser-window and genuinely-uncommitted

F.5q-c A ust_id denotes a HALF-OPEN interval whose span is its own precision, so the last covered slot of one window and the first of the next are contiguous. Comparing the two as strings reports a gap between every adjacent pair
F.5q-c A discontinuity between two published windows is a function of fields the documents carry — nothing declared anywhere is consulted
F.5q-c A chain nobody supplied and a publisher that has committed nothing look identical, so the report refuses rather than reporting a window unanchored
F.5q-c A rhythm is a CAPABILITY. A publisher that declares none promised none, and nothing is owed where nothing was promised — an event-driven stream is the ordinary case, not a deficient one
F.5q-c The two facts F.5p separates, applied to the declaration itself: declared-and-silent must not read like never-promised
F.5q-c The floor means the publisher promised NOTHING; a rhythm a reader cannot honour is a publisher that promised something, so it is refused rather than rounded down

F.5p.3 A member this verifier's version does not define is the RULESET term of R2: refused rather than dropped, and attributed to the READER — otherwise the first publisher to declare a newer member is called broken by every older reader
F.5p.3 ADVERSARIAL The attribution splits on whether the reader HOLDS the rule, never on the mere fact of a refusal

F clause 5 / §14 — a verifier that HOLDS the inputs and cannot evaluate the signature primitive MUST answer INDETERMINATE(unsupported_alg). It MUST NOT answer INVALID (inability is not guilt) and MUST NOT answer VALID (inability is not silence). The SAME document under a build that has the primitive verifies normally — both halves are normative, and an implementation is expected to run each under the build it describes.
